nodes.title: FA-32: explicit area arrays and improved layout defaults
nodes.body:
Array-based layout areas replace space-separated strings across the schema, engine, examples, docs and authoring skills. Reviewed layout defaults strengthen list text, keep compact metrics/quotes together, align numeric tables and place timeline labels beside their markers. Explicit region pins and authored overrides remain intact.

Validation: 2,327 core tests, 198 CLI tests and all 44 root checks passed locally. Official digest-pinned visual baselines cover 807 examples and 495 templates; changed artifacts were reviewed. Six candidate tarballs pass consumer TypeScript checks and eight browser suites (282 assertions). Gallery 3 source qualification is explicitly authorized; the published 0.19 control preserves its original runtime and uses three exact reviewed registry-test helpers.

nodes.title: Roadmap: native PowerPoint compatibility acceptance
nodes.body:
On September 15, 2026, the project owner requested that PowerPoint acceptance
gaps be split from the completed portable work and tracked on the roadmap.
This supersedes earlier draft wording that made native Office acceptance a
prerequisite for merging the shared header/footer implementation.

Core layout, browser preview, editing/undo and controlled XML export/reimport
can be accepted independently when their source, fresh-package, visual and CI
checks pass. This does not certify native PowerPoint behavior. Package release
and website adoption still require their own installed-registry verification.
Browser font-metrics failures remain separate engineering gates; moving Office
work here does not turn those failures into passing checks.

## Native Header/Footer objects (required end state)

OPF shared headers and footers **must** compile into native PowerPoint
Header/Footer objects: Office **Insert → Header & Footer**, the notes master,
and vendor `p:hf` date / slide-number / footer flags (and header where Office
exposes it). That is the furniture acceptance target for PowerPoint.

Published `@openpresentation/opf-pptx@0.8.1` does not do this. It paints
accepted furniture as ordinary slide shapes tagged `OPF_FURNITURE_V1` (plus a
common-slide manifest) and leaves vendor `p:hf` flags off
(`sldNum="0" hdr="0" ftr="0" dt="0"`). Notes-master placeholders remain
PptxGenJS defaults, not OPF-driven Header/Footer fields. Insert → Header &
Footer does not own the exported furniture.

Tagged-shape export, `OPF_FURNITURE_V1` provenance, and XML self-import are a
portable layout contract. They are **not** the intended PowerPoint end state
and do not close this issue. Do not treat furniture as done for PowerPoint.

## Remaining acceptance work

| Work | Current evidence and limitation | Acceptance required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recover the Windows Office test host | The [latest native handoff](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/pull/71#issuecomment-5673073461) requires user-reviewed recovery. Cleanup after the minimal picture control was not confirmed. | The Windows owner confirms recovery before further COM automation. No process killing or retries based on historical state. |
| Compile OPF headers/footers to native Office Header/Footer objects | PPTX 0.8.1 draws `design.header` / `design.footer` as ordinary slide text/pictures tagged `OPF_FURNITURE_V1`. Vendor `p:hf` stays off. The Office Header & Footer dialog and notes-master date/slide-number/footer placeholders do not receive OPF furniture. | Export date, slide number, footer text, and header where Office supports it as native Header/Footer objects (`p:hf`, notes master, Insert → Header & Footer). Tagged slide shapes are interim only. This row records the deferred converter requirement. |
| Open, save and reopen exported pictures and furniture | Nine exported files refused to open; valid ZIP/XML and portable browser tests did not establish Office acceptance. The missing slide-master declaration fix is already published in PPTX 0.8.0. Tagged-shape furniture is not native Header/Footer acceptance. | Re-run minimal and complete picture/header/footer controls after recovery, including the Header & Footer UI once native objects exist. Save/reopen in Office and inspect visible content and package changes. |
| Preserve furniture provenance through native edits | Controlled XML tests cover current text/images, cleared fields, missing/duplicate/changed tags, slide reordering and metadata disagreement. Actual Office handling of `p:cSld/p:custDataLst` and `OPF_FURNITURE_V1` is unverified. Those tags are not native Header/Footer objects. | Native edit/save/reimport controls retain current content and generated intent without resurrecting old words, including edits made through Insert → Header & Footer once that path exists. Review inheritance, empty/false definitions and damaged-tag fallback. Record formatting/geometry/crop reflow limits. |
| Native tab positions and mixed-size table paragraphs | Historical maximum tab drift is 0.0226745605469pt against a 0.02pt gate. Soft-wrapped mixed-size table runs can require conflicting 64px and 48px tab stops within one native paragraph. | Resolve the shared/native representation, preserve literal source whitespace and editable rich runs, and pass the unchanged native tolerance. No offsets, silent hard breaks or relaxed gates. |
| Native font and glyph identity | Family/style names do not prove which physical font supplied each glyph. Browser shaping and paint evidence is recorded separately. | Record permitted font bytes, actual substitutions, per-glyph physical identity where available, editable text and full-slide native comparisons on supported platforms. Restricted Aptos 4.40 remains excluded without compatible explicit permission. |
| Notes-master element order | The independent Open XML SDK rejects production ordering; diagnostic reordered copies pass, but upstream warns about PowerPoint behavior. | Compare both controlled outputs in recovered Office before changing production order. Preserve the existing output until native evidence supports a correction. |

For each completed item, retain the exact source/package identities, application
and OS versions, font hashes/licenses, original failures, native files and
reviewed images. Distinguish XML validity, semantic reimport, native editability
and pixel agreement in the result. Native findings do not invalidate separately
passing portable workflows, and portable results do not close native findings.

The broader [font roadmap](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/plans/font-roadmap.md) and
[ecosystem objective](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/plans/ecosystem-objective-2026-09-09.md) remain open. This split
does not change the default shaping backend or claim general Office parity.

Canonical committed copy: [docs/plans/powerpoint-acceptance.md](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/cursor/native-hf-roadmap-225d/docs/plans/powerpoint-acceptance.md) (draft [PR #92](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/pull/92)). PPTX companion: [PR #41](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf-pptx/pull/41).

nodes.title: Future: chart data from external spreadsheets (ChartDataSource) and a host dataResolver hook (descoped)
nodes.body:
**Status: descoped (owner decision 2026-10-01, release readiness program, [RR-18](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/programs/release-readiness/burndown.md)).** Charts whose data comes from an external spreadsheet are not part of this release. This issue records it as future work. Nothing here is scheduled. The issue is in core because it spans the schema, the preview ([opf-render](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf-render)), the export ([opf-pptx](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf-pptx)) and the editor.

## Current behaviour

- The schema allows `chart.data` to be either inline `ChartData` (`columns` and `rows`) or a `ChartDataSource` with `src` (an `asset:<id>`, HTTPS URL, data URI, relative or local path to CSV, TSV, JSON or XLSX), optional `sheet`, `range` (A1-style) and `columns` ([schema](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/spec/schemas/opf.schema.json) `ChartDataSource`, [schema reference](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/schema-reference.md#chartdatasource)). Such documents validate, edit and round-trip as authored.
- **Resolution is a host responsibility and no host hook exists.** The libraries are deterministic and never fetch, read files or resolve assets. [data-import.md](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/data-import.md) says OPF's existing `ChartDataSource` can declare a source reference, but source loading and refresh are a separate host responsibility. `createDataContent` and `parseTabularData` turn CSV/TSV/JSON text the host already read into inline `columns`/`rows` (an embedded snapshot, not a live link).
- **Preview (opf-render):** a chart with no inline `columns`/`rows` is not drawn as a chart: the catalog renderer returns null and the legacy "No chart data" placeholder shows (`src/charts.js`, `renderCatalogChart`).
- **Export (opf-pptx):** a chart with no inline data exports a placeholder frame ("Chart data is not inline, so it cannot be drawn here.") and reports the diagnostic `chart-data-unplottable` with `reason: "data-not-inline"` (`toPptxChartData`, `src/index.js`). No native chart part and no embedded workbook are written.
- **Editor:** edits the `ChartDataSource` fields; CSV/TSV/JSON import creates inline data with mapping and undo. Live source refresh is listed as remaining in [spec-editor-coverage.md](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/plans/spec-editor-coverage.md).

## What full support would need

1. **A resolver contract.** A host `dataResolver` hook, for example `(source: ChartDataSource, ctx) => Promise<ChartData> | ChartData`, accepted by the preview, the composition and export entry points and the editor, so a host with file or network access supplies inline data while the libraries stay deterministic and offline. Define sync versus async, caching, error and refusal diagnostics (a `chart-data-unresolved` code with the reason) and a security policy (no implicit network or file reads; same-origin and allowlist guidance for browsers).
2. **Resolution semantics.** How `asset:<id>` (the top-level assets registry), `sheet`, `range` and `columns` select a table; XLSX parsing (a dependency decision: size, licensing, browser safety); header-row and type inference; the existing chart data shape (category in column 0, numeric series after) as the target.
3. **Preview and export on resolved data.** Both engines already plot inline data, so after resolution they need no change; add tests that a resolved source equals the same inline chart (preview marks, native chart, embedded workbook).
4. **Provenance and round trip.** Keep the `ChartDataSource` reference in the exported PPTX provenance so re-import restores the source and not only the resolved snapshot, with a diagnostic when the snapshot and the source disagree; decide whether the native chart's embedded workbook mirrors the source file or the snapshot.
5. **Editor.** A host-provided picker and refresh action; staleness indication.
6. **Native check.** Supervisor-run PowerPoint confirmation that the exported chart and its workbook open and edit.

## Evidence

- Schema and docs: `ChartDataSource` in [opf.schema.json](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/spec/schemas/opf.schema.json) and [schema-reference.md](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/schema-reference.md#chartdatasource); host responsibility statement in [data-import.md](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/data-import.md).
- Coverage audit: [spec-editor-coverage.md](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/plans/spec-editor-coverage.md) (live source refresh remains).
- Preview and export behaviour: opf-render `src/charts.js` (`renderCatalogChart`), opf-pptx `src/index.js` (`toPptxChartData`, diagnostic `chart-data-unplottable`).
- Program: [release readiness README](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/programs/release-readiness/README.md#owner-decisions-of-2026-10-01).

nodes.title: Future: navigation and motion (transitions, builds/reveals, links between slides) (deferred, out of v1)
nodes.body:
**Status: deferred, out of v1 (owner decision 2026-10-01, release readiness program).** Navigation and motion are not part of the v1 release. This issue records what they would need. Nothing here is scheduled.

## Current behaviour

- **Schema:** there is no field for slide transitions, build/reveal steps (animations) or links between slides. A run can carry `link` (a URL string, see `TextRun.link` in [opf.schema.json](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/spec/schemas/opf.schema.json)); slides have `id`, `section` and `notes` but no internal link target.
- **Export (opf-pptx):** run `link` values with an `http(s):` or `mailto:` scheme become native hyperlinks; any other value is not exported as a link. No `p:transition`, no `p:timing` (builds), no slide-jump hyperlinks (`ppaction://hlinksldjump`) are written. Import ignores transitions and animations in third-party decks.
- **Preview (opf-render):** static SVG per slide; no transitions, builds or slide links. There is no presenter or player yet (RR-28 adds a deterministic slideshow with keyboard navigation and text notes, without motion).
- **Editor:** no controls for any of these.

## What full support would need

1. **Core (spec):** schema fields and catalog records for slide transitions (kind, duration, direction), builds/reveals on content items (order, effect, trigger: on click or after previous), and internal links (a run, item or shape linking to a slide `id`, "next", "previous", "first", "last"). Define determinism and reduced-motion rules, validation of dangling slide ids, and how pagination and composition-generated slides keep ids stable.
2. **opf-pptx:** write `p:transition` (with the `p14` extensions for modern effects), a `p:timing` tree for builds, and `ppaction://hlinksldjump` hyperlinks with relationships to the target slide parts; import them back into the new fields with specific diagnostics for unsupported effects. Native PowerPoint confirmation (supervisor-run) of each effect family, since timing XML is fragile.
3. **opf-render:** preview behaviour (a poster state per build step, or a stepped player), SVG/PDF export policy (final state; one page per build or not), and link handling (slide-jump targets in SVG and the player).
4. **opf-editor:** transition picker, build order panel, link target picker, undo as one patch, and a preview that steps through builds.
5. **Player (RR-28):** execute transitions and builds with `prefers-reduced-motion` respected; keyboard navigation of builds.
6. **Compatibility:** an effect catalog that maps to PowerPoint's effects one to one, so a deck never promises an effect the export cannot write.

## Evidence

- Schema: `notes`, `section` and `TextRun.link` in [opf.schema.json](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/spec/schemas/opf.schema.json); no transition or animation field.
- Export: opf-pptx `src/index.js` (run hyperlinks limited to `http(s)` and `mailto`).
- Program: [release readiness README](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/programs/release-readiness/README.md).

nodes.title: Future: rich speaker notes (formatted notes; plain-text notes stay) (deferred, out of v1)
nodes.body:
**Status: deferred, out of v1 (owner decision 2026-10-01, release readiness program).** Rich speaker notes are not part of the v1 release; plain-text notes stay. This issue records what rich notes would need. Nothing here is scheduled.

## Current behaviour

- **Schema:** slide `notes` is a plain `string` ("Speaker notes shown in presenter view", [opf.schema.json](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/spec/schemas/opf.schema.json)). There is no run formatting, list, link or image in notes.
- **Export (opf-pptx):** the notes string is written to the slide's notes page as plain text (`slide.addNotes`); carriage returns in notes are preserved with a fix-up. Import reads the notes text back as a string and drops formatting.
- **Preview (opf-render):** notes are never drawn; the renderer ignores them (they are also excluded from font coverage).
- **Editor:** edits the plain string. The presenter view in RR-28 will show text notes only.

## What full support would need

1. **Core (spec):** a notes representation with rich text (the same run model as slide text: bold, italic, links, lists), either a `notes` object beside the string form (backward compatible: a string stays valid) or a reference to a rich-text payload; validation and a migration note.
2. **opf-pptx:** write formatted runs and lists into the notes page body placeholder (the notes master text styles need to carry them), import them back into the rich model, and keep the plain string as the lossless fallback; native PowerPoint confirmation (supervisor-run) of the notes pane and Notes Page view.
3. **opf-render / player (RR-28):** render rich notes in the speaker view; decide whether the SVG/PDF export has a notes-page layout.
4. **opf-editor:** a rich-text notes editor with undo, reusing the rich text editing already in the editor.
5. **Fonts:** notes text uses the notes master fonts; the font policy (bundled or self-hosted, permissive licenses) applies to the speaker view.

## Evidence

- Schema: slide `notes` is `type: string` in [opf.schema.json](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/spec/schemas/opf.schema.json).
- Export: opf-pptx `src/index.js` (`slide.addNotes`).
- Program: [release readiness README](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/programs/release-readiness/README.md).

nodes.title: Layouts: bundle the 385 gallery-only layouts in core or keep a permanent subset; the 4 legacy font pairings have no OPF id (descoped)
nodes.body:
Found by the gallery tracker (RR-41, `docs/programs/release-readiness/gallery-tracker.md`): gallery items that the core catalogs do not bundle or do not define.

## Current behaviour

- **Layouts.** Core `spec/catalogs/layouts` bundles 100 of the 485 layouts pptx.gallery publishes: the 30 core structural layouts and the 70 legacy gallery slugs added by FF-55. The other 385 (the Dark master, for example `chart-1x-slideimage`; 24 of them are deprecated aliases from FF-52, such as `chart-1x-title-left`, replaced by `chart-1x`) are published only by the pptx.gallery layouts catalog. A document that names one of them resolves it online through the default catalog, but offline (core alone) only with an inline `catalogs.layouts.records` entry, which the gallery snippets add. All 485 are measured as working in audit A and in parity, so this is about where the records live, not about the engines.
- **Legacy font pairings.** The four legacy gallery font pairings (`bold-impact`, `classic-editorial`, `modern-professional`, `warm-storytelling`) have pages on pptx.gallery and are measured by audit B, but they have no OPF id in any catalog: their `app` value is not schema-valid, so the gallery does not publish them (FF-37).

## What full support needs

1. Layouts: decide (FF-37 proposal, step 2) whether core bundles all 485 gallery layouts or a curated subset. Bundling changes what composition and pagination can select, so it needs a renderer golden check and exporter measurement, not only catalog work. Then switch the kind to `mirror`, or record `subset` as permanent, and restore the narrative layout hints.
2. Font pairings: publish the four as schema-valid font-scheme records through the gallery-first sync, or retire their pages with redirects.

## Evidence

- `docs/programs/release-readiness/gallery-tracker.md` (RR-41): the `missing-spec` rows for layouts and font schemes.

nodes.title: Slide sizes and purposes: editor switches and a pptx.gallery aspect-ratio page (descoped)
nodes.body:
Found by the gallery tracker (RR-41, `docs/programs/release-readiness/gallery-tracker.md`): two kinds of value that the editor cannot switch and pptx.gallery does not show.

## Current behaviour

- **Slide sizes.** The schema's `DimensionPreset` has seven presets (`16:9`, `4:3`, `16:10`, `letter`, `a4`, `widescreen`, `standard`) and core composes each of them. Only `widescreen` is measured on the gallery configs (every theme uses it); the other six have no committed measurement yet (RR-43 adds it). opf-editor 0.11.0 has no slide-size switch: its switch operation covers 14 gallery dimensions (`SWITCH_DIMENSIONS`), and only a theme switch changes the dimensions, to the theme's own. pptx.gallery has no slide-size pages; its home page lists "Aspect ratios" as coming.
- **Purposes.** The 9 purpose records (`align`, `decide`, `educate`, `inform`, `persuade`, `pitch`, `plan`, `report`, `sell`) are document metadata (`purpose`). The editor has no purpose switch (the field is editable only in the JSON source), and pptx.gallery has no purposes pages (the gallery-side part is in the catalog-only records issue).

## What full support needs

1. An editor switch for `design.dimensions` presets and one for `purpose`, each one patch with exact undo and a preview refresh, as for the FF-16 dimensions.
2. A pptx.gallery aspect-ratio page with a card per preset.
3. Per-preset export and re-import tests (`p:sldSz`), parity on a non-widescreen config, and a native PowerPoint check of `4:3`, `letter` and `a4`.

## Evidence

- `docs/programs/release-readiness/gallery-tracker.md` (RR-41): the `missing-editor` and `missing-gallery` rows for slide sizes and purposes, and the `aspect-ratios` teaser row.
- `spec/schemas/opf.schema.json` (`$defs.DimensionPreset`), opf-editor `src/switches.js` (`SWITCH_DIMENSIONS`).

nodes.title: RR-48: enable the merge queue on the OpenPresentation main rulesets (owner action)
nodes.body:
**Owner action, from the RR-40 CI/CD study** (`docs/programs/release-readiness/ci-cd.md`, section 4; roadmap item M4; burndown RR-48).

**What is needed:** enable the GitHub merge queue in the `main` rulesets of OpenPresentation/opf, opf-render, opf-pptx and opf-editor (core: ruleset 24382980), with a batch size of up to 4. Only an owner can change rulesets. Merge queues are available to public organization repositories on the current plan.

**Agents prepare, before you enable it:**

- `merge_group:` triggers on the required workflows. They are harmless without the queue.
- A queue run that is the full coordinated ecosystem.
- Push-to-main runs reduced to a smoke check.
- Flake measurement and the quarantine file come first (RR-47), because one flaky check ejects a whole batch.

**Why (measured 2026-09-25 to 10-02):**

- Core ran 134 full ecosystem runs on `main` a week, at about 27 min each. 53 of them (40%) were cancelled by the next merge, so those main commits were never verified by the ecosystem.
- Pushes per merged PR were p90 6 to 10, mostly rebases and re-runs.
- Expected: about 2,400 runner-minutes a week saved, every `main` commit verified, and no rebase churn.

nodes.title: RR-50, RR-51: a GitHub App for cross-repository pin bumps, PRs and release tags (owner action)
nodes.body:
**Owner action, from the RR-40 CI/CD study** (`docs/programs/release-readiness/ci-cd.md`, sections 3 and 9; roadmap items L1 and L2; burndown RR-50 and RR-51).

**What is needed:** a GitHub App installed on OpenPresentation/opf, opf-render, opf-pptx and opf-editor with **contents: write** and **pull-requests: write** (and nothing else). Its app ID and private key go in core secrets. Agents cannot create Apps or secrets.

**What it enables:**

- **RR-50 (L1):** a bot-owned `ecosystem.lock.json` in core. A roller tries every repository's `main` and auto-merges a lock bump when they pass together. Coordinated changes use `Depends-On:` lines in the PR body. This replaces the hand-edited SHA pins and the throwaway pin branches. This week 77 of 181 sibling PRs edited CI pins, at least five PRs did nothing but repin, and 19% of analysed failures were pin or published-version coupling.
- **RR-51 (L2):** one release workflow that pushes the tags in order (core, then renderer and PPTX, then editor and the CLI), waits for each repository's own publish workflow, verifies the registry artefacts and provenance, and opens the next sibling's release-prep PR. Tags pushed with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger other workflows, so this needs the App token.

**What does not change:** npm trusted publishing. Each package is still published by its own repository's workflow through OIDC with `--provenance`. The App only creates tags and PRs.

The 0.12.0 train took 4 h 20 min from the core release PR to opf-editor on npm. The estimate with the release workflow is about 1 h 45 min.

nodes.title: Windows PowerPoint native runs deferred from the Mac mini session (RR-05, FF-12, FF-13, FF-27, FF-46)
nodes.body:
Tracking issue for every **native PowerPoint check deferred to the Windows host**. On 2026-10-02 the owner deferred Windows PowerPoint work while the release-readiness supervisor runs on the owner's Mac mini (no PowerPoint there). Each item below says what to run, the acceptance criterion it closes, and where the evidence goes. Program docs: [README](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/programs/release-readiness/README.md), [burndown](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/programs/release-readiness/burndown.md), [HANDOFF](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/programs/release-readiness/HANDOFF.md), [font burndown](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/programs/font-fidelity-everywhere/burndown.md).

## Host and run pattern (README invariants, HANDOFF "Native PowerPoint runs")

- Windows with desktop PowerPoint 365 (the 2026-10-02 runs used 16.0 build 20430). **Only the supervisor runs Office.** Agents build decks, a `manifest.json`, a `RUN.md` and a `compare.mjs`, and hand them over; they never open or automate Office.
- Decks are built with the **published** packages. Current set: `@openpresentation/opf` 0.12.0, `opf-render` 0.12.0, `opf-pptx` **0.12.2**, `opf-editor` 0.11.1 (0.11.2 in release), CLI 0.10.0. Record the versions in the evidence.
- Helpers (rebuild them; the 2026-10-02 copies lived in the old machine's scratch folder and are not in the repository):
  - `run-deck.ps1`: one deck per child `powershell.exe`, a **90 s deadline**, stops only its own child by PID.
  - `native-read-deck.ps1`: attaches to a running PowerPoint with `GetActiveObject`, opens **read-only** with `Presentations.Open(path, -1, 0, 0)`, reads runs, theme slots, `Presentation.Fonts`, geometry, fields and notes, exports slide PNGs, and **never saves, quits or kills PowerPoint**.
  - Run with `powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File …`; start PowerPoint first if it is not running. Never retry a native attempt in place; preserve failures as evidence.
- Evidence goes under `docs/evidence/<item>-native-<yyyymmdd>/`: a README, `compare.md` and `compare.json`. Do not commit decks, PNGs or absolute paths. Then update the burndown rows and regenerate the trackers (`pnpm build:gallery-tracker`, `pnpm build:font-tracker`).

## 1. RR-05 / FF-12: finish the native sample

The [CJK run](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/evidence/rr-05-cjk-native-20261002/README.md) passed 8 of 9 decks. `lang-ja-meiryo` failed `Presentation.Fonts`: PowerPoint added `Aptos`. That is the FF-05 behaviour, and those decks predate the fix in opf-pptx 0.12.1 (opf-pptx#152). The post-fix [FF-46 run](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/evidence/ff-46-native-0.12-20261002/README.md) reads no extra name on its Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Hindi and Thai decks, but it is not the FF-12 sample. Right-to-left already passed ([rr-05b](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/evidence/rr-05b-native-20261002/README.md)).

**Run:** one bounded sample, **at most 12 decks**, read-only, exported with opf-pptx 0.12.2. It must include at least:

- Carlito with code, chart, table and notes;
- the default scheme;
- a Japanese deck with Meiryo, which re-runs `lang-ja-meiryo`;
- an Arabic RTL deck;
- a monospace scheme;
- a per-slide override;
- CJK inside a Latin deck.

**Pass:** each deck's `Presentation.Fonts` names only its chosen families, theme references resolve to them, and any other name fails (FF-12 criterion). This closes FF-12 and RR-05.

## 2. FF-27: fields renumber and update natively

Already shown natively in [RR-42](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/evidence/rr-42-native-20261002/README.md): the 27 header/footer placeholders and 14 slide-number and date fields exist and have the right type. **Not shown:** that they renumber and update.

**Run:**

- A headers-footers deck that uses `slidenum` and a `datetime*` field. No gallery snippet exercises a `datetime*` field yet, so the deck has to add one.
- Open it read-only.
- **In memory only**, insert or move a slide and read the slide-number text back, and read the date field's text.
- Close without saving.

**Pass:** the numbers follow the new order and the date matches the chosen format. Then FF-27 is done, and RR-03 can close (it is the last open FF item of the ten).

## 3. FF-46 / RR-17: script, visual and code-table families to `documented-visual` ([opf#308](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/pull/308), draft)

**Families:**

- the 41 `script-gap` script faces
- `visual-gap`: Cambria Math and Segoe UI Emoji
- `code-table`: Symbol, Wingdings and Webdings

Didot is Apple-only and is measured on the Mac mini instead (opf#322).

**Measure:** for each family, measure the real font **in place** (`C:\Windows\Fonts`, never copied into a repository) against its bundled replacement:

- advance widths per style on the FF-44 script corpora
- line breaks
- vertical metrics
- outline and appearance (native PNG against the preview)
- coverage

The FF-46 native PNGs were lost with the old machine, so regenerate the FF-46 decks first. Then record acceptance through the builder mechanism in opf#308's Resume section and regenerate the font tracker. The draft PR's Resume lists the files and steps.

## 4. FF-13: font-embed attempt

**Criterion:** one supervised attempt from merged main, in a fresh directory, audited pass or fail. If it passes, the OPC audit shows exactly the chosen fonts embedded.

**Owner decision needed first:** the standing native rule is open read-only and never save. An embed attempt that uses PowerPoint's own "Embed fonts" needs a Save As of a copy into a fresh directory. Confirm that one bounded Save As of a copy, never overwriting the source, is allowed for this item, or rescope FF-13 to embedding done by the exporter.

## 5. Slide-size presets against PowerPoint's own sizes

opf-pptx writes A4 as `p:sldSz` 10689336 x 7562088 EMU (11.69 x 8.27 in, exactly the schema's inches). Compare it, and 4:3, 16:10 and letter, with the sizes PowerPoint's Design > Slide Size presets produce. Read them from a deck PowerPoint already made; do not save one. Record any difference. This is not a gate change, and the slide-size values already passed RR-42 on their own terms.

## 6. Open rows of [opf#87](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/issues/87): need an owner decision

The [2026-10-02 status comment](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/issues/87#issuecomment-5963559477) lists three open rows that no RR item covers:

- save and reopen of exported pictures and furniture
- furniture provenance (`OPF_FURNITURE_V1`) through a native edit and save
- native tab positions and mixed-size table paragraphs (the 0.0227 pt drift is above the unchanged 0.02 pt gate)

The first two need a save, which conflicts with the read-only rule. The owner decides whether they become post-v1 issues or new RR items, and whether saving a copy is allowed for them.

## Not Windows (for reference)

- **Mac mini (opf#322):** Didot, a PDFKit check of the vector PDF, Quick Look, Safari/WebKit and Keynote. The Keynote run is supervisor-only, read-only and never saved.
- **pptx-dev Windows e2e flakes:** `inspector-autosave.spec.ts:48` and `completion-keyboard.spec.ts:65` are GitHub-hosted CI work under RR-47 (pptx-dev#80) and need no host.

nodes.title: Roadmap: OpenDocument Presentation (.odp) import and export
nodes.body:
Roadmap item (owner request, 2026-10-09). Not scheduled.

## Goal
Read and write OpenDocument Presentation (`.odp`, LibreOffice Impress, ISO/IEC 26300) the way OPF reads and writes PPTX: deterministic and local, with no network, producing editable native objects.

## Shape
- `fromOdp(bytes)` / `toOdp(deck)` in a home to be decided: a new engine, or opf-pptx grown into an "office" engine. Decide against the five-package rule: a new package only for a real dependency or environment boundary.
- `convert("deck.odp", "deck.opf.md")` and `convert("deck.opf.md", "deck.odp")` through core `/node`, and `opf convert` on the command line, with `.odp` inferred from the extension.
- Fidelity bar like PPTX: text boxes, lists, tables, charts (native ODF charts with their data), images, backgrounds, headers and footers, speaker notes, fonts named and not embedded. Import of foreign `.odp` files turns unknown shapes into editable text with diagnostics, as `fromPptx` does.

## Why
ODP is the only other real office presentation format and an open ISO standard, so it fits OPF's open-format mission. It also gives LibreOffice users first-class support without going through PPTX.

## Open questions
1. Which package: a new engine or an extended opf-pptx?
2. Native verification: LibreOffice has to open the output, so define a headless check on Linux CI (`soffice --headless --convert-to pdf`), like the PowerPoint native checks.
3. Do charts map to ODF native charts with embedded data, or fall back to pictures at first?

nodes.title: Roadmap: import Marp and Slidev Markdown decks (fromMarp, fromSlidev)
nodes.body:
Roadmap item (owner request, 2026-10-09). Not scheduled.

## Goal
Read the Markdown slide dialects developers already write, [Marp](https://marp.app/) and [Slidev](https://sli.dev/), into OPF. Deterministic and local, and lossy only where the source carries HTML, CSS or Vue that OPF cannot represent.

## Shape (proposal)
- `fromMarp(text)` and `fromSlidev(text)` in core, next to `fromMarkdown` (`.opf.md`) and `fromYaml`, following the `fromX` naming rule.
- `convert("talk.md", "deck.opf.md", { from: "marp" })` and the same in `opf convert`. A plain `.md` file is never treated as an OPF deck, so the dialect has to be named, or detected from an unambiguous marker such as Marp's `marp: true` front matter.
- Findings report everything that could not be carried over: HTML, `<style>`, Vue components, clicks and transitions OPF lacks, and so on.
- Map the common features:

  | Feature | Marp | Slidev | OPF |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Slide separator | `---` | `---` | slides |
  | Speaker notes | `<!-- -->` | `<!-- -->` | `notes` |
  | Columns | — | layouts | regions |
  | Backgrounds | `![bg]` | layout `cover` / `image` | `background` |
  | Code | fences | shiki line focus | `code` |
  | Math | KaTeX | KaTeX | to decide |
  | Mermaid | — | Mermaid | to decide |
  | Headers, footers, pagination | `header`, `footer`, `paginate` directives | — | furniture with `{{slide.number}}` |

## The OPF dialect stays
`.opf.md` stays OPF's own Markdown. It is the lossless serialization of every OPF field: layouts, chart data, catalogs, variables and furniture, with `opf-slide` / `opf-block` fences for what Markdown can't express. Marp and Slidev are presentation dialects with their own HTML, CSS and Vue semantics, so they are import sources, not replacements. `toMarkdown` keeps writing `.opf.md`.

## Open questions for the owner
1. Import only, or also `toMarp` / `toSlidev` export so a deck can be presented in those tools? Export is lossy: no native charts, and layouts become CSS.
2. Should `convert`, `open` and the CLI auto-detect a Marp file (front matter `marp: true`)? Slidev has no reliable marker, so it would need `from: "slidev"`.
3. Are math (KaTeX) and Mermaid in scope as new OPF content kinds, or reported as lossy? They are the most common features in developer decks (see the Slidev and Marp roadmap research on this issue).

`fromPdf` is out of scope for the open toolkit: it needs paid OCR and AI and belongs to pptx.dev.

nodes.title: Roadmap (0.19): adaptive layouts: repeatable placeholders instead of list-2x/text-3x count variants
nodes.body:
## Problem
About 230 of the 280 catalog layouts are combinations of content kind (list, text, image, chart, number) × block count (1–6) × boxed × vertical × title position × item images. Example: `list-3x-box-vertical-title-left` is three list placeholders plus `design: { contentBox, contentDirection, titleAlignment }` and `composition.mode: "column"`. Every option except the count already exists as a design or composition field, and core already composes automatically (`composition.mode: "auto"`, or no layout at all). So "Nx" pins exactly the thing that should adapt: adding a fourth point means switching layouts.

## Proposal
1. **Repeatable placeholders:** `"placeholders": [{ "type": "title" }, { "type": "list", "repeat": { "max": 6 } }]`. One `list` layout accepts 1–N blocks and arranges them: 2 side by side, 3 in a row, 4 as 2×2, 5 as 3+2, 6 as 3×2.
2. **Variants as design settings, not ids:** `"layout": "list", "design": { "contentBox": true, "titleAlignment": "center" }`. A theme can set boxed once for the deck.
3. **Content-adaptive composition:** pick row, grid or column from block count and text length; pagination still never drops content.
4. **Single-list flow:** `"bullets": [...], "columns": "auto"` flows one long list into columns (the most common reason `list-2x` is used today).
5. **Intent-named layouts:** keep the meaningful ones (agenda, comparison, pillars, action plan, gallery, metrics, architecture stack) and drop the pure geometry combinations.

## Cost and sequencing
- Design the schema for the repeat placeholder and the composition rules first.
- Prototype in core.
- Then redo the catalog in pptx.gallery (it syncs into core; previews and the 819-config tracker change), the PPTX slide-layout mapping, the example decks and the sites.
- Breaking: no aliases pre-1.0.

Roadmap item, parked by the owner on 2026-10-09 (not in 0.18). Source: the Slidev/Marp gap research (comment on opf#506) and the CLI audit.

nodes.title: FF-46 follow-up: per-script sizeAdjust (Traditional Arabic letters vs digits/Latin)
nodes.body:
Split out of opf#361 at the release supervisor's request (2026-10-10).

**Problem.** `font-policy.json` `sizeAdjust` is one number per row, and opf-render applies it to every run drawn in the replacement face, letters, digits and Latin alike. Some proprietary families differ from their replacement differently per script. Traditional Arabic is the clearest case. Measured on the RR-38 basis (FF-44 corpus, real font read in place) against Noto Naskh Arabic:

- Arabic letters: 0.71–0.74
- Arabic-Indic and Persian digits: 0.90–1.02
- Arabic with a Latin word: 0.84
- the scheme's Latin: 0.84

The single factor 0.79 would make every FF-31 Latin string overhang natively: +6.7 % on the median string, +20.7 % at worst (175 pt on an 842 pt line), and the Persian digits +28.5 %. The smallest single factor with no overhang is about 1.015, so Traditional Arabic ships with no `sizeAdjust`.

**Proposal.** Add a per-script factor: a schema field on the policy row, keyed by script (Arabic letters), with digits and Latin left at 1. opf-render then splits runs by script when it applies it. For Traditional Arabic at 0.79 on the letters, this gives Arabic line ratios of 0.90 / 0.94 / 1.04 (min / median / max), and Latin keeps slack only.

**Notes.** The Thai families and Sakkal Majalla have Latin narrower still (0.57–0.65), so they would want their own Latin factor rather than 1.

Measurements: `ff46-sizeadjust-measurements.{md,json}` from the opf#361 work, to be committed with the #361 evidence.

- a `sizeAdjust` per fallback route when the requested family is Nirmala UI;
- per-script factors (see the per-script `sizeAdjust` issue);

nodes.title: textAsPaths: draw SVG text as glyph outlines (plan and drawbacks)
nodes.body:
The owner asked for a `textAsPaths: true` render option. With it, every `<text>` of a slide is drawn as glyph outlines (`<path>`), so the SVG needs no fonts at all. This issue is the plan and the list of drawbacks. It relates to RR-61 (embed only the faces a slide draws, plus `embedFonts: false`; branch `codex/rr-61-svg-font-embedding`) and to the glyph-subsetting issue OpenPresentation/opf-render#163.

## What it gives

- No `@font-face` data, no font loading and no fallback-font flash. The SVG looks the same in every browser, image viewer and design tool, with or without the fonts installed.
- Glyphs are exactly the ones the renderer measured. They come from the same fontkit shaping as layout, so browser shaping differences go away. Today those are worked around with `textLength` pinning, the FF-44 `text-spacing-trim` reset and the raster cluster pinning in `raster-text.js`.
- No font file ships with a shared SVG, only the outlines a slide uses.
- Small files. Measured on the core example decks (127 decks, 807 slides):
  - Outlines in font units are about 265–430 bytes per glyph: Carlito 428, Roboto 395, Intos 363, Montserrat 287, Tinos 265.
  - A slide draws 204 glyphs at the median (p90 333, max 610), with 32 distinct (p90 42, max 52).
  - With one `<path>` per distinct glyph in `<defs>` and a `<use>` per occurrence, a slide comes to about 25–40 KB. Inline paths without reuse come to about 80 KB at the median and 260 KB at most.
  - For comparison, office-pack slides embed 2.4 MB of faces on average after RR-61 (15.1 MB before), and an SVG with no fonts is about 10 KB.

## Drawbacks

1. **The text stops being text.** No selection, copy, find-in-page or translation, and screen readers lose the per-element text. The plan keeps the slide's `aria-label` and adds a `<desc>` with the slide text in reading order, plus `aria-label` on each text group. That is still weaker than real text.
2. **Not an editing surface.** A WYSIWYG caret, selection highlight and IME composition need live text in a real font. The editor would use outlined text for thumbnails, the slide sorter, presenter and export previews, not for the element being edited. The `data-opf-text-start/end` trace stays on the groups, so hit testing by box still works.
3. **The vector PDF loses real text.** `svgToPdf` of an outlined SVG draws paths: not selectable, not searchable, no tagged text, and larger files. PDF export must keep rendering from the `<text>` SVG. `svgToPdf` should warn when it receives an outlined SVG (a `data-opf-text-as-paths` marker).
4. **Small-size rendering is softer.** Browsers hint and subpixel-render text, but draw paths with plain geometric anti-aliasing. That is fine at slide size; at thumbnail size text looks a little lighter. resvg already draws text as outlines, so PNG output barely changes.
5. **Colour and bitmap glyphs.** COLRv0 layers can be outlined (one path per layer and palette colour). COLRv1 (Noto Color Emoji) and bitmap glyphs (sbix, CBDT) cannot. Those clusters stay `<text>`, and RR-61's used-faces rule then embeds just that face. A diagnostic `text-as-paths-kept-text` reports it.
6. **Licensing.** A face whose OS/2 `fsType` forbids embedding (restricted license) is not outlined. It stays `<text>` with a diagnostic, the same rule the PDF export applies.
7. **Size for some scripts.** CJK and other large-repertoire scripts have many distinct glyphs, at about 1–3 KB each. A text-heavy CJK slide can reach a few hundred KB, which is still far below one CJK face (5–10 MB).
8. **CPU.** It is a second layout pass over each text element. Glyph paths are cached per face and glyph id, and the cost must be measured on the example decks before the option is offered to live previews.
9. **New baselines.** It is a new output mode, so it needs its own golden baseline. Existing goldens and the 0.1 px browser text gates stay on `<text>` output, untouched.

## Design

- **API.** `renderSvg(deck, { fonts, textAsPaths: true })` and the same option on `renderSlideSvg`. It needs a fonts handle with a registry (Node or browser `loadFonts`). Without one it throws `text-as-paths-needs-fonts`, because the portable width estimate has no outlines. Default off.
- **Where.** A post-pass over each slide's content markup in `renderResolvedSlide` (`src/svg.js`), before font embedding. Once no `<text>` remains, the RR-61 used-faces rule embeds nothing by itself.
- **Layout.** Reuse the vector PDF's SVG text layout: `layoutText` in `src/pdf-text.js` (text chunks, bidi isolates, per-character fallback, fontkit shaping with features and language, `textLength` adjustment) over a `FontLibrary` from `src/pdf-fonts.js`, built from `registry.exportFaces()`. Both are synchronous once built, and they already run in the browser for `/export-browser`. The renderer has decided every position, so this only turns positioned runs into geometry.
- **Output.**
  - Each `<text>` becomes a `<g>` that keeps its fill, opacity, stroke, `<a>` link and `data-opf-*` trace. Each tspan segment becomes a nested `<g>` with its `data-opf-text-start/end`.
  - Glyphs are `<use href="#g-<face>-<gid>" transform="matrix(s 0 0 -s x y)">`. The horizontal scale absorbs `lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs"`.
  - Paths are in font units with integer coordinates, so output stays byte-stable.
  - Underline and strike-through become rects from the face's `post`/`OS/2` metrics.
- **Fallbacks.** Colour/bitmap glyphs and restricted faces stay `<text>` (drawbacks 5 and 6). `font-feature-settings` from `font-compatibility.js` are honoured by `layoutText`.

## Phases

1. Latin, bidi and decorations, links and trace groups. Test file `test/text-as-paths.mjs`:
   - every `<text>` is replaced;
   - glyph ids match `layoutText`;
   - resvg PNGs of the outlined and `<text>` SVGs agree within the raster tolerance on the core example decks;
   - output is byte-stable.
2. Colour-glyph and `fsType` fallbacks with their diagnostics. Script corpora, including Arabic, Indic and CJK.
3. Accessibility: `<desc>` and group labels, checked with axe in the browser suite.
4. A browser suite: outlined vs `<text>` ink inside the existing 0.1 px containment gate (`accepted-text-browser` method). A separate golden baseline through the `regenerate-goldens` workflow.
5. Consumers: opf-editor thumbnails and slide sorter, an opt-in for the player and `<opf-deck>`, and an "Outline text" choice for SVG downloads.

## Open questions

- The name: `textAsPaths` or `outlineText`.
- Whether `/export-browser` PNG export should use it by default, since it removes the font-loading wait.

nodes.title: fontkit RangeError on an empty last glyph when glyf ends the file (upstream report drafted)
nodes.body:
**fontkit throws `RangeError` on a TrueType font whose last glyph is empty and whose `glyf` table ends the file.**

`TTFGlyph._getCBox` reads a 10-byte glyph header at the glyph's `loca` offset even for an empty glyph (`loca[i] == loca[i+1]`). In a normal font that reads the next glyph's header: harmless, though the bounds are wrong. When the empty glyph is the last one and `glyf` is the last table in the file, the read runs past the end: `RangeError: Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView` from `DecodeStream.readInt16BE`. Any `layout()` that touches the glyph (its `advanceWidth` getter goes through `_getMetrics` → `_getCBox`) throws.

## Where it bites us

- hb-subset writes `glyf` last, and a space (empty) is often the last glyph of a small subset. RR-65 (opf-render#184) works around it: `glyfBeforeLastTable` in `src/font-subset.js` moves `glyf` before the other tables.
- Third-party fonts can have the same layout, for example subsets from other tools passed as SVG `@font-face` data. They would still crash:
  - the browser PDF export (`/export-browser` reads `@font-face` data with fontkit through `FontLibrary`);
  - the vector PDF;
  - the RR-64 outliner.

## Options here

1. Guard locally: in `FontLibrary.addData` (and wherever we `fontkit.create` caller-supplied bytes), pad a copy of the bytes with 12 zero bytes when `glyf` is the last table, before parsing.
2. Report upstream (draft below) and pick up the fix when released.

## Draft upstream report (foliojs/fontkit), not posted; awaiting the owner's OK

> **TTFGlyph._getCBox reads past the end of the font for an empty last glyph**
>
> fontkit 2.0.4. For a TrueType font whose `glyf` table is the last table in the file and whose last glyph is empty (`loca[n-1] === loca[n]`, for example a space), calling `font.layout(text)` on text that uses that glyph throws `RangeError: Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView` from `DecodeStream.readInt16BE`, via `TTFGlyph._getCBox` → `_getMetrics` → `advanceWidth`.
>
> `_getCBox` decodes `GlyfHeader` at `loca.offsets[id]` without checking for an empty glyph (`loca.offsets[id] === loca.offsets[id + 1]`). `_decode` does check. Fonts produced by HarfBuzz's subsetter (hb-subset) write `glyf` last, so subsets whose last glyph is a space trigger it reliably.
>
> Suggested fix: in `_getCBox`, return an empty `BBox` (or the glyph's hmtx-only metrics) when the glyph has no outline data, as `_decode` does.
>
> Repro: subset any TTF to the characters "ab " with hb-subset (space last), then `fontkit.create(bytes).layout('ab ')`.

Found in the pre-0.18 audit.

nodes.title: Future: native PowerPoint video (p:video) export, import and preview playback (descoped)
nodes.body:
**Status: descoped (owner decision 2026-10-01, release readiness program, [RR-18](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/programs/release-readiness/burndown.md)).** Native PowerPoint video is not part of this release. This issue records it as future work. Nothing here is scheduled.

## Current behaviour

- `video` is a valid content kind in the OPF schema (`slides[].video`, `content[].video`, item `type: "video"`; a string, `asset:<id>` or an `Asset` with `src` and metadata; see [content-payloads.md](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/content-payloads.md)).
- **Export (this repo):** a video payload exports as a placeholder group: a frame rectangle, a play badge (ellipse), a play triangle and a centred caption (title, then source). The frame and the badge carry a hyperlink to the source when it is an `http(s)` URL, so it stays usable in PowerPoint. No `p:video`, no media relationship, no embedded or linked video part is written. The code says so: "Native video embedding is not attempted" (`src/index.js`, `addMediaPayload`).
- **Round trip:** the placeholder shapes carry `OPF_MEDIA_V1` provenance (`src/media-provenance.js`, [document-roundtrip.md](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf-pptx/blob/main/docs/document-roundtrip.md)), so an unchanged group re-imports as the original `video` block; an edited group degrades to text with `invalid-media-provenance`. Data-URI videos have no exported part and are omitted with `media-provenance-omitted`.
- **Preview (opf-render):** the same placeholder, drawn as SVG (a bordered surface, a 72 px play badge and a caption). There is no playback and no `<video>` element, by design (deterministic, static SVG).
- **Editor:** edits the `video` fields (source, metadata). No playback ([spec editor coverage](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/plans/spec-editor-coverage.md) lists video playback as remaining).

## What full support would need

1. **Export:** write a native video picture shape (`p:pic` with a video file reference and the `p14:media` extension, a poster frame as the picture), with the media part and relationship, either embedded (size and privacy limits, a licensing and byte-budget decision) or linked (`TargetMode="External"`, which PowerPoint plays only when the link resolves). Remote `http(s)` URLs, such as YouTube links, are not playable as native media; PowerPoint's online-video construct is different and needs its own research and native confirmation.
2. **Poster frame and fallback:** a deterministic poster image (from `Asset` metadata or a placeholder) so the file looks right without playback; keep the current placeholder as the fallback for sources that cannot be embedded.
3. **Import:** read native video and online-video shapes back into `video` blocks with source, caption and poster, and keep diagnostics for sources that cannot be represented.
4. **Preview playback (opf-render):** decide whether the preview stays a placeholder (static SVG, deterministic) or offers a host hook for an embedded player; at minimum a poster frame.
5. **Native verification:** supervisor-run PowerPoint confirmation (open, play, save, reopen) on the Windows host, as for other native constructs.
6. **Provenance:** keep `OPF_MEDIA_V1` stable or version it.

## Evidence

- Spec: the `video` kinds in [opf.schema.json](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/spec/schemas/opf.schema.json); coverage statement in [spec-editor-coverage.md](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/plans/spec-editor-coverage.md).
- Export: `addMediaPayload` and `src/media-provenance.js` in this repository.
- Preview: opf-render `src/svg.js` (the `video` payload draws the `media-1x` placeholder).
- Program: [release readiness README](https://github.com/OpenPresentation/opf/blob/main/docs/programs/release-readiness/README.md#owner-decisions-of-2026-10-01).

nodes.title: List import: a description resized in PowerPoint becomes part of the entry text
nodes.body:
Found in the native check of opf-pptx#235 (PowerPoint 16.0 build 20430).

Import tells a list's description lines from its text lines by font size: an unbulleted line of the entry's own size continues the entry, and a smaller one is its description (`src/index.js`, the comment above `joinRich`). If a user resizes a description in PowerPoint to the entry's size or larger, the description comes back as a continuation of the entry text:

```
source:  {text: "With a description", description: "about it"}
edited:  description run size 15.37 -> 36 in PowerPoint
import:  ["With a description", {text: "about it", fontSize: 36, color: "#F0F0F0"}]
```

The `color` is a knock-on effect: once the line counts as text, it is compared against the text look recorded by opf-pptx#235 (`listRuns`), not the description look.

**Proposed fix:** when the slide record is present, classify lines by the record (the export knows which line numbers are description lines; record them next to `lists`/`listRuns`). Keep the size heuristic only for decks without provenance.

**Acceptance:** a description resized or recoloured in PowerPoint stays a description and comes back with only the edited value.

nodes.title: Use loadFonts subsetWasm/shapeWasm for SVG downloads and outlined text
nodes.body:
**Browser downloads don't use the renderer's HarfBuzz opt-ins yet.** These are `loadFonts({ subsetWasm })` (RR-65, opf-render#184) and `loadFonts({ shapeWasm })` (RR-64 phase 2, opf-render#185).

- **SVG downloads embed whole faces.** Standalone SVG downloads made with the browser fonts handle still embed each used face whole. The Node handle cuts them to the slide's glyphs: an office-pack slide averages 59 KB instead of 2.4 MB over the core example decks. The browser handle does so only with `subsetWasm`, the URL of `harfbuzzjs/dist/harfbuzz-subset.wasm` the host serves.
- **Outlined text is shaped with fontkit.** With `textAsPaths` / 0.18's `text: "paths"`, browser outlines are shaped with fontkit unless the handle has `shapeWasm` (`harfbuzzjs/dist/harfbuzz.wasm`). fontkit differs from Chromium on Thai, Bengali, Khmer, Myanmar, Lao, Syriac and Japanese combining marks.

Proposal for the gallery (same as opf-editor):
- Serve both WASM files next to the font files (pinned from the installed harfbuzzjs, like the vendored fonts).
- Pass them to the browser `loadFonts` used for downloads and exports.
- Live canvas previews keep `embedFonts: false` (0.18 `text: "system"`).

nodes.title: e2e: move other JSON-editor fills to fillJson (latent CodeMirror focus-timer race from #73)
nodes.body:
Follow-up from #101 (#73). Playwright's `fill()` on an unfocused CodeMirror editor can race CodeMirror's 10 ms focus-update timer. If the browser reports `fill()`'s select-all after that timer, the select-all is dropped and the new text is inserted at offset 0, in front of the old document.

#101 adds `fillJson()` and `focusJson()` in `tests/e2e/json-editor-helpers.ts`. They wait for `cm-focused` before filling. #101 applies them only to `code-editing.spec.ts`.

Other specs whose first action fills an unfocused JSON editor carry the same latent race: `exact-source`, `preview-editing`, `json-options`, `fonts` and possibly others (`rg "fill\(" tests/e2e`). None of them has failed yet. Moving them to `fillJson` is optional hardening.

Acceptance: every JSON-editor fill in tests/e2e goes through `fillJson` (or a documented exception), and the e2e suite stays green.

nodes.title: Roadmap: PDF to OPF import (fromPdf) with OCR and AI recovery
nodes.body:
Roadmap item (owner decision, 2026-10-09): **PDF to OPF import (`fromPdf`) belongs in pptx.dev, not the open-source toolkit.** It needs OCR and AI layout and semantics recovery (paid APIs, paid models), and the open toolkit is deterministic and local, with no network and no models.

## Shape
- Upload a PDF to pptx.dev. OCR, layout and AI semantics recovery turn it into an OPF deck: slides, titles, lists, tables, charts recovered as data where possible, and images. Then validate and render it with the open toolkit.
- Output is an `.opf.json`/`.opf.md` deck with findings that say what was recovered and with what confidence.
- Complements the open toolkit's `fromPptx`, and the planned `fromMarp`/`fromSlidev` (OpenPresentation/opf#506) and ODP import (OpenPresentation/opf#505).
